title: Working with JSON from an API

contentBlocks.body: APIs send data as JSON **text**. `JSON.parse(text)` turns that text into JavaScript objects and arrays; `JSON.stringify(value)` turns a value back into text. Until you parse it, a response is just a string.

Real API data is messy. Fields go missing, values are null, and sometimes the response is an error message instead of what you expected. Three tools keep your code from crashing:
- `try/catch` around `JSON.parse`, which **throws** on invalid text
- optional chaining `?.`, which gives `undefined` instead of an error when something along the path is missing
- `??` to supply a default when a value is `null` or `undefined`
Pick only the fields your screen needs and give each a clear default. The rest of your app then works with a small, predictable shape instead of the whole raw response.
`??` only replaces `null` and `undefined`. `||` also replaces `0`, `""`, and `false`, which is wrong when 0 is a real value (a score of 0, a price of 0).
Numbers can arrive as strings ("7" instead of 7). Check types with `typeof value === "number"` before trusting them.

**Worked example.** JSON parsing checks syntax and creates JavaScript values. It does not prove the object follows your API contract. Validate the fields and ranges you depend on before calculating with them.
A type assertion in TypeScript also does not validate incoming JSON at runtime.

**Try a small change.** Try a syntactically valid response with count set to a string.

Then complete the independent check below without copying the example. Explain the boundary case in words before running it.

payload.explanation: Invalid JSON throws, so wrap JSON.parse in try/catch when the text comes from outside your code.
Optional chaining stops at the missing profile and returns undefined instead of trying to read name from it.

payload.text: const count = data.count ____ 0; // use 0 only when count is null or undefined

knowledgeItems.prompt: Write parseUsers(json). The text looks like {"data":{"users":[...]}}. Return [{ id, name, email }] for each user with a numeric id. name comes from profile.name (default "Unknown") and email defaults to null. Invalid JSON or a missing users array returns [].
